chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: He narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from Saif ibn Amirah, from Abdullah ibn Ubaydullah, from Abu Basir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: When the month of Ramadan approached, with three days remaining from Sha'ban, he said to Bilal: 'Call the people.' So the people were gathered, and he ascended the pulpit, praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: 'O people, this is a month that has come to you, and it is the master of months. A night in it is better than a thousand months. The gates of Hell are closed in it and the gates of Paradise are opened in it. So whoever is granted the opportunity of this month and is not forgiven, may Allah distance him. And whoever is granted the opportunity and [fails to gain forgiveness for] his parents, may Allah distance him. And when I am mentioned in his presence and he does not send blessings upon me, [and] he is not forgiven, may Allah distance him.'
ai.seo_question: What are the virtues of Ramadan and the consequences of not seeking forgiveness during this month according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A'mal* underscores the unique spiritual gravity of Ramadan as 'master of months,' linking the closing of Hell's gates to the imperative of familial piety and *Salat al-Nabi*. It reflects the Shia emphasis on the interconnection between ritual worship, honoring parents, and remembering the Prophet as essential pathways to divine forgiveness during this sacred time.
